headline: Bengaluru's AI agent momentum is exploding—your moment to ship real agentic systems is right now.
why_now: With GitHub activity at 96, project potential at 96, and career value at 95, agentic workflows are the hottest hands-on AI trend in 2026. Bengaluru is India's deep-tech hub, and job demand at 85 signals companies are actively hiring agent builders. Strong Hugging Face activity (92) and community buzz (84) give you a ready ecosystem to learn from and contribute to.
study: Master the LLM tool-use fundamentals: read OpenAI function calling docs, Anthropic's tool use guide, and the ReAct paper to understand planning + action loops.
Build with a production framework: pick LangGraph or CrewAI and complete their official quickstart plus 2 tutorial projects end-to-end.
Study agent architectures: implement ReAct, Plan-and-Execute, and multi-agent collaboration patterns in a Jupyter notebook using LangChain.
Learn evaluation and reliability: read DeepEval and AgentBench papers, then add tracing with Langfuse or Arize Phoenix to a sample agent.
Join Bengaluru meetups: attend a PyData Bangalore, Bangalore AI, or LlamaIndex/CrewAI local workshop to find collaborators.

build.title: Bengaluru CivicOps: Multi-Agent Urban Issue Resolver
build.description: A multi-agent system where a Planner agent triages Bengaluru civic complaints (potholes, power outages, garbage), a Researcher agent pulls data from BBMP and BESCOM public APIs and news feeds, and a Reporter agent drafts a citizen-ready response with action steps. It demonstrates agent orchestration, tool calling, memory, and real-world API integration—exactly what Bengaluru startups and civic-tech teams are building.
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean README, architecture diagram, and setup instructions
Live Streamlit demo deployed on Hugging Face Spaces or Railway
Blog write-up on Hashnode or Dev.to showing agent traces and a before/after comparison
Short 2-minute Loom demo video walking through a real complaint scenario

publish: Post the project on Hacker News (Show HN) with a clear headline and the live demo link—agent projects regularly hit the front page.
Share a build-in-public thread on X and LinkedIn tagging LangChain, LangGraph, and Bengaluru AI community accounts; Bengaluru founders scroll LinkedIn heavily.
Submit a talk proposal to Bangalore AI Meetup, PyData Bangalore, or JSConf India—offering to demo live builds gets accepted faster than slides.
Contribute a PR or tutorial to LangGraph or CrewAI docs and mention it in your README; maintainer visibility transfers credibility to you.
skills: LLM tool use and function calling
risks: Agent frameworks are shifting fast—LangGraph, CrewAI, and AutoGen all compete, so avoid over-investing in one proprietary pattern; keep your core logic framework-agnostic.
Real-world API reliability (BBMP/BESCOM endpoints can be flaky or undocumented) may force scope cuts—have a mocked-data fallback from day one.
Evaluation is still an open problem; without good traces and assertions, your agent will silently regress as you iterate—budget time for evals, not just features.
confidence: Very high—signals are strong across GitHub, Hugging Face, jobs, and Bengaluru's ecosystem, and 'create_agents' is a clear, achievable scope for someone with an agent-builder profile.
